Title: RecoverAgent: Intent-Preserving Recovery from Indirect Prompt Injection in Tool-using LLM Agents
Abstract: Tool-using LLM agents execute multi-step tasks by iteratively reasoning and interacting with external tools. However, they are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection (IPI), where adversarial instructions embedded in tool outputs can divert benign user intents into unsafe actions or unintended goals. Existing defenses mainly prioritize reducing unsafe behaviors, while paying limited attention to preserving the original user intent. As a result, safety improvements may come at the cost of interrupting execution or distorting benign task goals. This reveals a key gap in current LLM-agent defenses: the trade-off between safety and intent preservation remains largely underexplored. We propose RecoverAgent, an intent-preserving recovery framework that enables agents to continue execution after detecting unsafe intermediate responses. Instead of terminating the task, RecoverAgent rewrites unsafe responses into safe and executable alternatives while maintaining alignment with the original user intent. Experiments on R-Judge, InjecAgent, AgentHarm, ASB, and BadAgent demonstrate that RecoverAgent reduces attack success and harmful behaviors while substantially improving trajectory completion and intent fidelity compared to other defenses under IPI.
Major_Contribution_Result: RecoverAgent is an intent-preserving recovery framework for tool-using agents under IPI: after a monitor flags unsafe intermediate responses, a recovery module rewrites them into safe executable alternatives aligned with the original user goal instead of only refusing. Experiments on R-Judge, InjecAgent, AgentHarm, ASB, and BadAgent are reported to reduce attack success and harmful behaviors while improving multi-round trajectory completion and intent fidelity versus refusal-heavy and other baselines. On clean AgentHarm-benign trajectories without IPI, Online RecoverAgent reports higher continuity metrics than several baselines (e.g., Llama3.1-8B Benign Score 64.92 / PNA 63.73 / LLM Judge SR 58.90).
Research_Limitations_Challenges: The authors state recovery adds computation/latency and depends on monitor accuracy (misses or unnecessary recoveries can affect normal execution). Evaluation covers three multi-round IPI objectives plus ASB-IPI, which is narrower than the full attack space. The approach assumes unsafe behavior mainly from observation contamination rather than malicious user intent. High-risk domains may need explicit authorization before executing recovered actions. Experiments focus on single-agent settings with moderate horizons; long-horizon, multi-agent, and recovery-exploiting adaptive attackers remain future work.
Critics: This mitigation paper targets the safety–utility trade-off after IPI by recovering trajectories rather than only blocking them. Quantitative gains are benchmark- and model-specific; clean-run table values above should not be over-generalized as universal utility scores. For LLM-agent security evaluation, it covers post-detection continuity under observation contamination, but is not a full gate-governed lifecycle across supply-chain, MCP, or multimodal threats.
